Being around people in authority or uniform

Threat.value: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations

vignette: Alejandro, a 26-year-old Latin American man, had experienced unspeakable trauma when he was subjected to torture during a visit to his home country five years ago. The event left deep scars that have lingered in his psyche and daily life ever since. A former hotel maid, Alejandro now works as a maid at a bustling downtown hotel in the United States. His current job is fraught with triggers that make each day an exhausting ordeal. The trauma began when Alejandro was arrested by authorities under false pretenses during a family visit to Mexico. He was held incommunicado and subjected to brutal interrogation techniques designed to extract information he didn't possess. The experience was both physically and psychologically devastating, leaving him with an overwhelming sense of helplessness and fear. Since returning to the United States, Alejandro has struggled to navigate his daily life without constantly reliving that harrowing period. One of his most potent triggers is encountering media content related to his torture. Every time he sees news reports or movies featuring scenes of violence or police brutality, a flood of memories comes rushing back, leaving him feeling disoriented and anxious. Even the sight of similar cars to those used by authorities during his arrest can set off intense flashbacks. Alejandro's daily routine at work has become a minefield. He dreads interactions with management, who often wear uniforms or carry themselves in authoritative manners reminiscent of his captors. The constant need to avoid such figures has led him to isolate himself from colleagues and supervisors, causing tension on the job. His attempts to distance himself from potential threats have also resulted in missed opportunities for career advancement and a general sense of disconnection from his peers. One of Alejandro's most significant coping mechanisms is smoking cigarettes, which he believes helps calm his nerves and distract him from intrusive memories. However, this habit has taken a toll on his health, leading to frequent respiratory issues that sometimes interfere with his work performance. At night, Alejandro struggles to sleep soundly. He often wakes up in the middle of the night, compelled by an intense need to check whether he is safe. This ritualistic behavior stems from a deep-seated fear that something terrible might happen if he doesn't stay vigilant. Unexpected touches also cause him to react with alarm and fear. Simple gestures like a colleague patting his shoulder or a client placing their hand on his arm can trigger panic attacks, making social interactions particularly difficult. Alejandro's trauma has profoundly impacted his relationships as well. After his divorce, he found it increasingly challenging to form new connections due to his guarded nature. His ex-wife had become suspicious of his frequent disappearances and secretive behavior, eventually leading to their separation. Now, Alejandro is deeply isolated, struggling to trust others and fearing the emotional vulnerability that comes with forming close bonds. What frightens Alejandro most is the unpredictability of his triggers and the relentless fear they evoke. The threat he perceives from strangers in ordinary situations has made it nearly impossible for him to engage fully in daily life without constant vigilance. He worries about losing control or breaking down at any moment, which has left him feeling trapped by his own mind. Despite these struggles, Alejandro finally decided to seek help after a particularly harrowing episode at work where he was unable to complete his tasks due to an overwhelming sense of anxiety and panic. He is hopeful that therapy can provide strategies to manage his symptoms better and regain some control over his life. His most fervent hope is to find a way to live without constantly reliving the horrors of his past, allowing him to reconnect with others and reclaim his sense of safety and peace.
